<SUMMARY>The period of May 8-15, 2026, was dominated by high-stakes geopolitical engagements, particularly President Donald Trump's summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing, where discussions centered on trade, Taiwan, Iran, and export controls. The ongoing war with Iran continued to escalate, with President Trump stating the US-Iran ceasefire is on life support, causing significant energy market instability and economic impacts globally. In the semiconductor sector, Intel Foundry secured a major deal with Apple for M-series and A-series chips, while significant investments in AI computing and foundry development, including Cerebras's $5.5 billion IPO and SpaceX's $55 billion foundry plan in Texas, highlighted the accelerating technological race. Critical minerals, especially rare earths and cobalt, remained a key area of competition, with China tightening control over its producers and the US pursuing supply deals in Africa, while the Netherlands opposed US proposals to restrict ASML's exports to China.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>The declaration that the US-Iran ceasefire is on life support and the rejection of a peace proposal indicates a high risk of further escalation in the Iran conflict, threatening broader energy market stability and increasing costs for US businesses. China's move to tighten control over its rare earth producers, coupled with the Pentagon's stated urgency to diversify rare earth supply, signals an impending intensification of competition over critical mineral supply chains. The potential for the Netherlands to oppose US export control proposals regarding ASML's sales to China poses a risk to the cohesion of Western technology export strategies.</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:**
President Donald Trump met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing for a summit addressing trade, the Iran war, and Taiwan. The leaders engaged in high-level discussions aimed at stabilizing their trading relationship and navigating geopolitical uncertainties. China seeks A.I. independence, which could influence future technological cooperation. Lam Research announced plans to hire over 1,000 professional engineers in Taiwan in 2026 due to mounting customer demand for AI chips. HDRE is set to deploy containerized AI compute centers paired with energy storage systems in Australia and Japan, with cooperation projects expected to finalize in the first half of 2026. Taiwan intends to launch a green power spot market by late 2026 or early 2027 to better allocate renewable generation and reduce electricity pressures on energy-intensive industries. Alibaba's AI spending is projected to exceed goals based on signs of payoff. The Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026 is open for entries across Southeast Asia. HostColor.com announced new data center locations in Asia to deliver RDP server hosting services. Intel's preliminary Apple deal is exerting pressure on Samsung's foundry ambitions. Taiwan's economy is experiencing a surge due to AI demand, strengthening its position in the global supply chain. Japanese chip maker Calbee is sending some of its packaging into austere black-and-white due to war-related shortages impacting civilian life.

**Africa:**
Madagascar has announced a constitutional referendum and elections, signaling potential democratic changes. Kenya's President Ruto explicitly rejected a "raw mineral export" future for Africa. The US and Europe are struggling to counter China’s expanding grip on Africa’s rare earths, a challenge highlighted by China’s Huayou planning to buy an Africa-focused Australian miner in a lithium rush. A US Cobalt Refinery Supply Deal With Congo (EGC, EVelution Energy, and Trafigura) is under analysis for 2026.

**Europe:**
British inference chip startup Fractile Ltd. closed a $220 million Series B funding round co-led by Accel, Factorial Funds, and Founders Fund. HostColor.com announced new data center locations in Europe to deliver RDP server hosting services. Kneat reported a record revenue for Q1 2026 of $18 million, an 18% increase from Q1 2025, with gross profit growth accelerating to 28% year-over-year. Mattr Corp. reported strengthening composite technologies performance, driving sequential growth and an improved full-year outlook for Q1 2026. NanoXplore Inc. reported its financial results for Q3 2026.

**Americas:**
Eight Directions Technology Limited announced entering into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Quartzsea Acquisition Corporation. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife are donating $108.3 million in computing time from CoreWeave to universities for AI research, an initiative that also bolsters CoreWeave, an AI cloud company in which Nvidia has invested heavily. Cerebras Systems Inc. priced its stock at $185 per share ahead of its IPO, then saw its stock almost double to $350 a share on its opening day, raising $5.5 billion. HostColor.com announced new data center locations in the U.S. and South America to deliver RDP server hosting services. Euro Sun Mining Inc. announced board changes, appointing Charles Wachsberg as a director. Condor Energies Inc., a Canadian-based company focused on Central Asia, released its unaudited interim results for Q1 2026. ExGen Resources Inc., a Canadian company, adopted semi-annual financial reporting. NanoXplore Inc., a Canadian graphene company, reported its financial results for Q3 2026. Foundry limits and policy gaps are impacting semiconductor capacity. SpaceX is moving forward with a plan to build a $55 billion semiconductor foundry in Texas. The Manual Wafer Aligner Market is projected to reach US$ 1.58 billion by 2033, growing at an 8.8% CAGR from 2026-2033. Intel Foundry reportedly secured Apple's M7 production on 18A-P in 2027 and future smartphone chips on 14A.

**Oceania:**
HDRE announced its entry into the AI compute dispatch market by building containerized compute centers paired with energy storage systems in Australia and Japan.

</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Europe:**
The Netherlands opposes a US proposal to further restrict chip giant ASML from the China market. ASML's global dominance in lithography technology was highlighted, detailing how the company achieved its market position. TSMC, a Taiwanese company, predicts the global chip market will reach $1.5 trillion by 2030, driven by AI growth.
</LITHO>
<REE>
**Asia:**
China moved this week to take tighter control of its rare earths producers amid escalating tensions with Washington over various issues, including trade and Iran. China's Huayou plans to acquire an Africa-focused Australian miner in a strategic move related to lithium.

**Africa:**
Kenya’s President Ruto has rejected a future based on "raw mineral exports." China’s Huayou, a Chinese company, is in the process of acquiring an Africa-focused Australian miner as part of its lithium acquisition strategy. A US Cobalt Refinery Supply Deal With Congo, involving EGC, EVelution Energy, and Trafigura, is being analyzed for 2026. Reports indicate that the U.S. and Europe are struggling to counter China’s expanding influence over Africa’s rare earths and critical minerals.

**Americas:**
The Pentagon has less than eight months to address and potentially break China’s rare earth grip. USA Rare Earth, Inc. announced its financial and operational results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026.
</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:**
US President Donald Trump held a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Discussions included efforts to stabilize the trading relationship and economic cooperation. Taiwan's economy is surging due to demand for AI technologies. The Steel Architectural Awards ASEAN 2026 program has opened for entries across Southeast Asia.

**Americas:**
HostColor.com has launched new data center locations in the U.S. and South America. Euro Sun Mining Inc. has announced changes to its board of directors. Condor Energies Inc. released its first-quarter 2026 results. ExGen Resources Inc. adopted semi-annual financial reporting. Mattr Corp. reported its first-quarter 2026 operational and financial results. NanoXplore Inc. reported its third-quarter 2026 financial results.

**Africa:**
Madagascar is proceeding with a constitutional referendum and elections.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Europe:**
President Zelenskyy met with the CEO of Palantir as Ukraine continues to intensify its utilization of AI in warfare operations.

**West_Asia:**
The war in Iran is causing an energy crisis that is impacting global markets. AI is playing a major role in the ongoing conflict in Iran. The deteriorating US-Iran relations could destabilize global oil markets and heighten geopolitical tensions. The War with Iran is increasing costs for U.S. businesses. Economic warfare is shaping the US-Iran conflict.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>
The week's intelligence highlights a complex global environment marked by high-level US-China diplomatic efforts that yielded few immediate breakthroughs on contentious issues like trade and the escalating Iran war. The AI and semiconductor industries are experiencing rapid growth and significant investment, driving geopolitical competition for foundry capacity, talent, and critical minerals. China's efforts to secure its rare earth supply and pursue AI independence underscore a strategic decoupling from Western supply chains. The ongoing conflict in Iran continues to exert substantial pressure on global energy markets and businesses, with explicit statements from President Trump indicating a worsening situation. Efforts to diversify critical mineral supply chains, particularly in Africa, are gaining traction amidst China's dominant position.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to embark on a five-nation tour, including the UAE and four European nations (Netherlands, Sweden, Norway), with discussions in the UAE specifically focusing on strengthening energy security. India’s data center industry is exploring sustainability, policies, and infrastructure during Entrepreneur India’s Tech and Innovation Summit 2026, aiming to power AI, efficiency, and scale. A DBS economist stated that India is losing investor attention to Asia’s AI-electronics surge, though the foreign direct investment slowdown is not a major concern; however, the economist recommended that India integrate more into supply chains and adopt pragmatic approaches to Chinese investment. The Trump-Xi meeting could test India’s strategic positioning as a counterweight to China’s influence in the Indo-Pacific.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed the Iran war during their Beijing summit. Vice President JD Vance denied President Trump's own words that the US economy was not a major factor in seeking a resolution with Tehran. President Trump will seek China's assistance with the Iran conflict, although Beijing is unlikely to fully comply, preferring to maintain its economic and military ties with Iran. President Trump stated that the US-Iran ceasefire is on life support after rejecting a peace proposal, indicating deteriorating US-Iran relations that could destabilize global oil markets and heighten geopolitical tensions. The Iran war is increasing costs for U.S. businesses and causing a global energy crisis. AI plays a major role in the war on Iran. A Cooperation Council statement declared that "Iranian attacks have also led to a sharp loss of confidence by the Council states in Iran," urging Iran to rebuild trust. Prime Minister Modi is likely to seek increased energy supplies from the UAE during his visit. The energy squeeze behind the Iran war is also linked to the AI boom. The Middle East Crisis is impacting global energy markets, with severe energy sector damage reported in Qatar. Economic warfare is a defining feature of the US-Iran conflict. Netanyahu's ruling coalition in Israel submitted a proposal to dissolve parliament, paving the way for early elections. The Iran war energy shock drives interest in ethanol and other biofuels across hard-hit Asia.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
Geopolitical tensions are expected to remain high, primarily driven by the unresolved US-China trade and security issues and the escalating Iran war. The semiconductor industry will likely see continued heavy investment and competition, with significant capital flowing into AI chip development and advanced foundry construction, particularly in the US and Taiwan. The scramble for critical minerals, especially rare earths and cobalt, will intensify, with China's strategic consolidation and Western diversification efforts in Africa defining this competitive landscape. The energy crisis spurred by the Iran war will continue to be a dominant factor, impacting global inflation and shaping diplomatic efforts to secure alternative supplies, while the military application of AI in conflicts like the Iran war and Ukraine indicates a new era of warfare.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
